content.value_statement: Vague coding-agent tasks drift, repeat work, and report success without evidence. Ariadne Loop turns them into bounded loop specs with verifiers, stop rules, and human gates.
actual_capabilities: Turns rough notes or issue text into a structured loop snapshot.
Defines inspect, act, verify, and decide cycles for coding agents.
Adds concrete verifiers, stop rules, rollback behavior, and human approval gates.
Produces agent packets for Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, and similar tools.
Documents report contracts for ongoing loop supervision.
References optional Ariadne Loop CLI commands for users who have the CLI installed.
limitations: Does not install or run the Ariadne Loop CLI by itself.
Does not validate remote GitHub, release, or Pages state without user-provided evidence.
Does not replace human approval for commits, deploys, payments, or external messages.
Works best when the user provides clear goals, constraints, and verifier expectations.

use_cases.title: Convert Issue Into Agent Work
use_cases.description: Prepare a bugfix or refactor issue as a bounded task with gates and rollback rules.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Reports
use_cases.description: Define report contracts so repeated agent turns show evidence, failed gates, and next actions.

use_cases.title: Resume Long Coding Threads
use_cases.description: Create a compact handoff that preserves current state, recent progress, constraints, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Loop Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Ariadne Loop spec for this task: [task]. Include goal, current state, verifiers, and stop rules.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a GitHub Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this issue title and body into an executable agent loop. Include risks, constraints, and human approval gates.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Resumable Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this long work log and create a resumable loop packet for Codex or Claude Code. Preserve blockers and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Supervise a Running Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these agent progress reports against the loop spec. Decide whether to continue, stop, request human input, or roll back.

output_examples.input: A vague request to fix checkout failures.
output_examples.output: A loop spec with the bugfix goal, reproduction command, passing test gate, rollback rule, and approval points.

output_examples.input: A GitHub issue describing a risky deployment change.
output_examples.output: An agent packet that separates inspection, implementation, verification, rollback, and human deployment approval.

output_examples.input: Several agent progress reports from a stalled refactor.
output_examples.output: A supervision decision that identifies failed gates, missing evidence, and the next bounded action.

best_practices: Provide the current repository state, known constraints, and expected external effects.
Use verifiers that produce observable evidence, such as command output or validated artifacts.
Require human confirmation before commits, pushes, deployments, billing, or external messages.
anti_patterns: Do not treat an agent status claim as proof without a verifier.
Do not merge unrelated refactors into the loop contract.
Do not ask the agent to perform external effects without explicit approval gates.

faq.question: What does Ariadne Loop create?
faq.answer: It creates structured loop specs and agent packets for bounded coding-agent work.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: The skill itself is guidance. It may suggest optional CLI commands when the Ariadne Loop CLI is already installed.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is written for Codex, Claude, Claude Code, OpenClaw, and similar coding agents.

faq.question: Can I use it without the CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill tells the agent to produce the snapshot and packet directly when the CLI is unavailable.

faq.question: What makes a verifier strong?
faq.answer: A strong verifier produces evidence, such as command output, a validated artifact, or a readback from a remote target.

faq.question: Does it handle risky actions?
faq.answer: It requires human confirmation before commits, pushes, releases, deployments, deletions, payments, and external messages.
